name: The Amalfi Coast
tagline: Cliffside villages, lemon terraces and a coast best seen from the sea.
distinctive: A UNESCO-listed coastline of steep terraces, pastel villages and gardens hung above the sea. It rewards arriving slowly, by boat where possible, and staying long enough to ignore the itinerary.

image.alt: Positano rising from the sea on the Amalfi Coast at dusk

moodNotes.sea: Days start with a swim from the rocks and end with a boat back along the cliffs.
moodNotes.art: Ravello's villa gardens, the cathedral at Amalfi and the Greek temples of Paestum within a day's reach.
moodNotes.lifetime: Few coastlines anywhere are as dramatic, and the terraces at dusk live up to every picture you have seen.
moodNotes.weekend: Possible as a long weekend from Europe, but the transfer from Naples means it rewards more time.
moodNotes.wellness: Slow mornings, sea swimming and long lunches set the pace.

seasonNote: Many hotels on the coast are seasonal and close through the winter. July and August are the most crowded months.

arrival.transfer: Allow roughly 75 minutes to two hours by road to Positano or Ravello, depending on traffic. In season, a car to the port and a boat along the coast is an elegant alternative.
arrival.groundNote: The coast road is narrow and winding, and it is congested in summer. Parking in the villages is scarce and expensive.

driving.note: We do not recommend self-driving here in season. The coast road is demanding, parking is scarce, and the best views are from the water.

transfer.label: Private driver and boat
transfer.why: A local driver takes the coast road so you can look at it, and a private boat reaches the grottoes, beaches and Capri.

stay.name: Le Sirenuse
stay.why: A long-established family-run hotel above Positano's beach, known for its terraces facing the town and sea. It is a natural base for boat days.

watchWhy: A water-resistant diver's watch you can wear from a morning swim to dinner on the terrace without a second thought.
aromaWhy: Lemon leaf and neroli reflect the coast's terraced citrus groves and suit a sea-facing room.

days.title: Arrive by sea
days.text: Transfer from Naples and settle in. In the evening, walk down through Positano to the beach for an early dinner by the water.

days.title: Ravello's gardens
days.text: Have a driver take you up to Ravello for the gardens of Villa Rufolo and the belvedere of Villa Cimbrone. Return for a late swim.

days.title: A day on the water
days.text: Charter a boat for the coves and grottoes of the coast, with lunch at a beach restaurant reached only by sea.

moreDays.title: Capri
moreDays.text: Take an early boat to Capri and leave before the day crowds peak.

moreDays.title: Paestum
moreDays.text: Drive south with a driver to the Greek temples of Paestum, some of the best preserved anywhere.

moreDays.title: The Path of the Gods
moreDays.text: Walk the Sentiero degli Dei in the cool of the morning, with good shoes, water and a guide if you prefer.
